theorems.name: Two-candidate S4-equivariant edge-transport classification
theorems.statement: A tetrahedrally equivariant involutive transport attached to an overlap edge and exchanging its endpoints is uniquely either the endpoint transposition (ij) or the complementary double transposition (ij)(kl).

theorems.name: Proper half-turn face closure
theorems.statement: The three proper double-transposition transports around any tetrahedral face are the nonidentity elements of V4 and multiply to the identity.

theorems.name: Reflective face twist
theorems.statement: The three endpoint reflections around a face have odd composite, so every triangular face carries nonzero chirality holonomy.

theorems.name: Determinant parity is chirality parity
theorems.statement: In the standard three-dimensional tetrahedral representation, determinant equals permutation sign; under an orthogonal carrier map Q, Q J_n Q^{-1}=det(Q) J_{Qn}, so proper versus improper transport is exactly the local J-sign bit.

theorems.name: Symmetric phase selection
theorems.statement: Proper double-transposition transport realizes the flat zero residual and a global signed J; endpoint-reflection transport realizes the uniform all-face twist and endpoint torsion.

selection_rule: If future native overlap transport is formalized as orientation-preserving, the flat global-J phase is forced. If it is reflection-like, the uniformly twisted projective-Euler phase is forced.
